questions: Does line_loss_events fall to 0 at mass 0.4 kg, or does one loss per run remain?
Does max_error move below about 0.06 m, or does it stay pinned at the off-track floor? If pinned, is the limit lag or top speed?
Does steering_oscillation stay below about 0.2 with the lowest yaw inertia, or does the robot overshoot the bends?
If line losses are cleared but progress stays low, is the next step a sensor bar move to y = 0.06 m (lag) or wheel_radius 0.035 with wheel_track 0.10 (top speed)?

intent: Test the minimum mass (0.4 kg) alone, as the Integrator's contingency rule requires after one line loss per run persisted at 0.5 kg with max_error pinned at the off-track floor. Only mass changes from the iteration 4 design. Expected result: line_loss_events falls toward 0 and max_error drops below about 0.06 m. If both happen, the next iteration moves the sensor bar to y = 0.06 m for lead. If line losses persist, the next change is to lag or top speed, not mass.
learning: Iterations 0 to 4 show that pitch, footprint, track and mass each leave one line loss per run and max_error at the 0.06 m floor. Mass is the last untested variable on yaw inertia. If 0.4 kg also fails, the line-loss cause is probably the sensor lag, so the next test moves the bar forward, and progress should then be checked against the top-speed hypothesis.
rationale: Race evidence from iteration 4 (mass 0.5 kg, 0.016 m footprint, 20 mm pitch at x = -0.04 to +0.04, y = 0.04, track 0.10 m, wheel radius 0.03 m) shows that the mass change did not clear the line loss. All 60 trials again ended off_track, with line_loss_events at 1.0 on every development track. max_error sits at the off-track floor (0.0613 oval, 0.0645 s-bend, 0.0677 slalom). Progress is 0.11 to 0.16 and steering_oscillation is low (0.07 to 0.16), so the robot drifts off the line rather than oscillating. Score moved only from 53.2728 to 53.5316, which is within noise of earlier designs. Across iterations 0 to 4, sensor pitch (10 to 20 mm), footprint (0.012 to 0.016 m), track (0.12 to 0.10 m) and mass (0.8 to 0.5 kg) have all left the single line loss per run and the max_error floor unchanged. The Integrator's rule for this case is: if one line loss per run remains with max_error still at the floor, yaw inertia is not enough, so try the minimum mass of 0.4 kg before any other change. I follow that rule. I change only mass, from 0.5 to 0.4 kg (the allowed minimum), and keep the iteration 4 geometry. This keeps the test attributable. I do not move the sensor bar forward yet: the Integrator's lag rule applies only when line_loss_events reaches 0, and that has not happened. Expected result: a further 20 percent cut in yaw inertia may reduce the line loss, but the effect is probably small, because mass has moved little on max_error so far. If line losses still persist, the next candidate will test lag (sensor bar at y = 0.06 m) or top speed (wheel_radius 0.035 with wheel_track 0.10), depending on which evidence appears. The off-track floor cannot be raised: max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) stays at 0.06 m for every allowed body_width.
